title: Endangered Formosan Salmon Return to a Lost Mountain Creek
summaryZh: 瀕危櫻花鉤吻鮭重返司界蘭溪，下月可望野外繁殖
summaryHi: संकटग्रस्त फ़ॉर्मोसा सैल्मन सिहजिएलान नाले में लौटी, अगले महीने प्राकृतिक प्रजनन की उम्मीद।
summaryEs: El salmón de Formosa en peligro vuelve al arroyo Sihjielan y podría desovar en libertad el mes próximo.
summaryJa: 絶滅危惧のサクラマス（タイワンマス）が司界蘭渓に戻り、来月にも野生で産卵の見込み。
summaryKo: 멸종 위기 대만 연어가 쓰제란 개울에 돌아와 다음 달 자연 산란이 기대된다.
summaryEn: Endangered Formosan landlocked salmon have returned to Sihjielan Creek and may breed in the wild next month.
paragraphs: Taiwan's endangered Formosan landlocked salmon has re-established itself in Sihjielan Creek, a remote stream in central Taiwan that lies on the ancestral lands of the Atayal people. Shei-Pa National Park Headquarters says the fish are expected to spawn naturally next month.

Atayal oral history describes the creek as once home to a thriving wild population, but environmental change and human development gradually wiped it out. Previous efforts to reintroduce the species there failed because the habitat had been badly degraded.

Nature, oddly, provided the solution. Around a decade ago, floodwaters destroyed a check dam downstream, and natural erosion of the riverbed slowly recreated the deep pools and gravel beds the salmon depend on. In September last year, the park airlifted 240 ten-month-old fish to the upper creek by helicopter, the first time it had used this method.

Earlier this month, a research team set off from the Atayal village of Sqoyaw, trekked 3.1km along a mountain trail, waded 5.5km upstream and camped overnight before snorkelling a 600m stretch around the release site. They counted 117 adults, giving a visible survival rate of 48.75 percent, and observed courtship and pairing. Because fish were also spotted beyond the survey area, the true rate may be above 50 percent.
The park says the creek is the final piece in restoring the salmon across its historic range in the Dajia River basin. It will now monitor young fish and the population's resilience to floods.
The Formosan landlocked salmon is a rare fish. It lives only in cold mountain rivers in Taiwan. There are not many left.
Long ago, these fish lived in Sihjielan Creek, in central Taiwan. The Atayal people tell old stories about them. But people changed the land, and the fish disappeared.
Last year, park workers used a helicopter to carry 240 young fish to the top of the creek. This was the first time they did this.
This month, a team walked a long way to the creek and slept there for one night. They swam in the cold water and counted 117 adult fish. Some fish were in pairs.
The fish may lay eggs next month. The park will keep watching them.

牠們剩下的數量不多。
很久以前，這種魚生活在台灣中部的司界蘭溪。
泰雅族人流傳著有關牠們的古老故事。
但人們改變了土地，這種魚就消失了。
去年，國家公園的工作人員用直升機把 240 尾幼魚運到溪流上游。
這是他們第一次這麼做。
這個月，一支團隊走了很遠的路到溪邊，並在那裡過了一夜。
他們在冰冷的溪水中游泳，數到 117 尾成魚。
有些魚成雙成對。

paragraphs: Taiwan's endangered Formosan landlocked salmon has come back to Sihjielan Creek, a mountain stream on the traditional land of the Atayal people. Shei-Pa National Park says the fish could start breeding in the wild next month.

According to Atayal stories, the creek was once full of these salmon. However, changes to the environment and human building work slowly destroyed their home, and the fish vanished. Earlier attempts to bring them back failed.

About ten years ago, a flood broke a small dam on the creek. Over time, the water shaped new deep pools and beds of small stones, which are exactly what the salmon need. So in September last year, the park used a helicopter for the first time to carry 240 young fish, about ten months old, up the valley.

This month, researchers started from the Atayal village of Sqoyaw, hiked 3.1 kilometres, waded 5.5 kilometres up the river and spent a night there. Then they snorkelled along a 600-metre section and counted 117 adult fish. Some were already pairing up.
The park will now watch for baby fish and check whether the population can survive floods. Full results are expected at the end of the year.

雪霸國家公園表示，這些魚下個月可能開始在野外繁殖。
根據泰雅族的傳說，這條溪過去到處都是這種鮭魚。
然而，環境的改變和人類的建設工程慢慢破壞了牠們的家，這種魚也就消失了。
之前讓牠們回歸的嘗試都失敗了。
大約十年前，一場洪水沖毀了溪上的一座小水壩。
隨著時間過去，溪水塑造出新的深潭和小石礫床，這正是鮭魚所需要的。
因此在去年九月，國家公園首次用直升機把 240 尾約十個月大的幼魚運上溪谷。
這個月，研究人員從泰雅族的思源（Sqoyaw）部落出發，健行 3.1 公里，溯溪涉水 5.5 公里，並在那裡過夜。
接著他們沿著 600 公尺長的河段浮潛，數到 117 尾成魚。
有些已經開始配對了。
國家公園接下來會觀察是否有小魚出現，並確認族群能否撐過洪水。
完整結果預計在年底出爐。

sentZh: 台灣瀕危的櫻花鉤吻鮭已在司界蘭溪重新建立族群，這是一條位於台灣中部、泰雅族祖居地上的偏遠溪流。
雪霸國家公園管理處表示，這些魚預計下個月會自然產卵。
泰雅族的口述歷史描述這條溪曾經有繁盛的野生族群，但環境變遷和人為開發逐漸讓牠們消失殆盡。
先前在此復育這個物種的努力都失敗了，因為棲地已嚴重劣化。
奇妙的是，大自然提供了解答。
大約十年前，洪水沖毀了下游一座攔砂壩，河床的自然侵蝕慢慢重新塑造出鮭魚賴以生存的深潭和礫石床。
去年九月，國家公園以直升機將 240 尾十個月大的魚空運到溪流上游，這是首次採用這種方法。
本月稍早，一支研究團隊從泰雅族思源部落出發，沿山徑跋涉 3.1 公里、溯溪涉水 5.5 公里並紮營過夜，接著在放流地點周圍 600 公尺的河段浮潛調查。
他們數到 117 尾成魚，目視存活率為 48.75%，並觀察到求偶和配對行為。
由於在調查範圍外也發現了魚，實際存活率可能超過 50%。
國家公園表示，這條溪是讓鮭魚重返大甲溪流域歷史分布範圍的最後一塊拼圖。
接下來將監測幼魚以及族群抵禦洪水的韌性。

paragraphs: In a notable conservation success, Taiwan's endangered Formosan landlocked salmon has re-established a foothold in Sihjielan Creek, a remote headwater on Atayal ancestral land in central Taiwan. Shei-Pa National Park Headquarters anticipates the first wild spawning there as early as next month.

According to Atayal oral tradition, the creek once sustained a flourishing population, which was gradually eradicated by environmental change and human encroachment. Subsequent attempts at reintroduction foundered on a degraded habitat that could no longer support the fish.

Ironically, it was a natural disaster that paved the way for recovery. Roughly a decade ago, floodwaters swept away a downstream check dam, allowing the riverbed to erode and gradually restore the deep pools and gravel beds essential for spawning. Seizing the opportunity, the park last September airlifted 240 juvenile salmon to the upper reaches by helicopter, a first for the agency.

This month's survey was an expedition in its own right: researchers set out from Sqoyaw village, hiked 3.1km, waded 5.5km upstream and spent a night in the valley before snorkelling a 600m stretch. They recorded 117 adults, a visible survival rate of 48.75 percent, along with courtship behaviour. Since fish were sighted outside the surveyed section, the actual figure may well exceed half.

Officials describe the creek as the final piece in restoring the species throughout its historic range in the Dajia River basin. Monitoring will now focus on juvenile emergence and how resilient the population proves to be against floods.
sentZh: 在一項引人注目的保育成就中，台灣瀕危的櫻花鉤吻鮭已在司界蘭溪重新站穩腳步，這是台灣中部泰雅族祖居地上一條偏遠的源頭溪流。
雪霸國家公園管理處預期，最快下個月就會出現當地首次的野外產卵。
根據泰雅族的口述傳統，這條溪曾養育繁盛的族群，後來因環境變遷和人類侵擾而逐漸絕跡。
後續的復育嘗試都因棲地劣化、無法再支持魚類生存而觸礁。
諷刺的是，為復育鋪路的竟是一場天災。
大約十年前，洪水沖走了下游的一座攔砂壩，讓河床得以侵蝕，逐漸恢復產卵所必需的深潭和礫石床。
國家公園把握這個機會，去年九月以直升機將 240 尾幼鮭空運至上游，這是該機關的首次。
本月的調查本身就是一趟遠征：研究人員從思源部落出發，健行 3.1 公里、溯溪 5.5 公里，在溪谷過夜後再浮潛調查 600 公尺的河段。
他們記錄到 117 尾成魚，目視存活率為 48.75%，並觀察到求偶行為。
由於在調查河段外也有目擊紀錄，實際數字很可能超過一半。
官員形容這條溪是讓該物種重返大甲溪流域整個歷史分布範圍的最後一塊拼圖。
監測工作接下來將聚焦於幼魚的出現，以及族群面對洪水時展現的韌性。

paragraphs: Conservationists in Taiwan are celebrating a significant milestone: the endangered Formosan landlocked salmon has successfully recolonised Sihjielan Creek, a secluded tributary on the ancestral territory of the Atayal people. Shei-Pa National Park Headquarters expects the fish to begin spawning naturally next month.

The species' disappearance from the creek, preserved in Atayal oral history, is a familiar story of ecological decline: a once-abundant population was steadily eliminated by environmental degradation and human development. Crucially, earlier reintroduction programmes proved unsuccessful precisely because the habitat itself remained unsuitable.

The turning point came unexpectedly. When floodwaters demolished a downstream check dam about ten years ago, the resulting erosion gradually reshaped the riverbed, recreating the deep pools and gravel beds on which spawning salmon rely. Capitalising on this, park authorities last September deployed a helicopter, for the first time, to transport 240 juveniles to the upper reaches.

The follow-up survey required considerable effort: a 3.1km trek, a 5.5km wade upstream and an overnight stay, followed by snorkelling along a 600m section. The team counted 117 adults, implying a visible survival rate of 48.75 percent, and documented courtship and pairing. As fish were also observed beyond the survey boundaries, the genuine figure is likely to be higher.

Officials regard the creek as the final piece of a broader effort to restore the salmon across its historic range in the Dajia River basin. The next priority is to monitor juvenile emergence and assess the population's resilience to flooding, with full results due at year's end.
sentZh: 台灣的保育人士正在慶祝一個重要的里程碑：瀕危的櫻花鉤吻鮭已成功重新拓殖司界蘭溪，這是泰雅族祖居領域上一條隱密的支流。
雪霸國家公園管理處預期，這些魚下個月將開始自然產卵。
這個物種從溪中消失的經過保存在泰雅族的口述歷史中，是一個常見的生態衰退故事：曾經數量豐富的族群因環境劣化和人為開發而逐漸被消滅。
關鍵在於，先前的復育計畫之所以失敗，正是因為棲地本身仍不適合。
轉捩點出乎意料地到來。
大約十年前，洪水摧毀了下游的一座攔砂壩，隨之而來的侵蝕逐漸重塑河床，重新形成產卵鮭魚所依賴的深潭和礫石床。
國家公園當局把握這個機會，去年九月首次動用直升機，將 240 尾幼魚運送到上游。
後續調查耗費了相當大的心力：跋涉 3.1 公里、溯溪涉水 5.5 公里並過夜，接著沿 600 公尺的河段浮潛。
團隊數到 117 尾成魚，代表目視存活率為 48.75%，並記錄到求偶和配對行為。
由於在調查範圍之外也觀察到魚，真實數字可能更高。
官員認為這條溪是讓鮭魚重返大甲溪流域歷史分布範圍這項更大工作的最後一塊拼圖。
下一個重點是監測幼魚的出現，並評估族群對洪水的韌性，完整結果將於年底公布。
